name: The Narrows Compact
description:
The Narrows Compact controls a critical smuggling corridor through Detroit's old salt mine tunnels — a network of passages running beneath the city that connects the waterfront to the interior districts without ever surfacing. In a city where surface movement is monitored by corporate drones and Axiom checkpoints, an underground highway is worth its weight in contraband. The Compact charges for access and provides guides through the maze of tunnels that would kill an unescorted traveler through collapse, flooding, or simply getting lost in the dark.

The crew numbers about fifty, split between tunnel guides, guards, and the maintenance workers who keep the passages navigable. They're led by a rotating council of three tunnel bosses, each responsible for a section of the network. The Compact is disciplined by necessity — one careless member could collapse a passage and destroy months of route maintenance. New members undergo a six-month apprenticeship learning the tunnel system before they're trusted to guide cargo or people.

The Compact smuggles everything: augments, weapons, drugs, data, food, medicine, and people. They don't discriminate by cargo — if it fits in the tunnels and the client pays, it moves. This moral flexibility has made them essential to Detroit's underground economy and simultaneously despised by everyone who's ever been victimized by the goods they transport. The Compact's response to moral criticism is a shrug: they move things from point A to point B. What happens at either end isn't their problem.

Their most lucrative service is people smuggling. Refugees, fugitives, corporate defectors, and anyone else who needs to move through Detroit without being seen pay premium rates for guided passage. The Compact has never lost a client in transit — their record is a point of genuine pride and their best marketing tool.
ideology: Neutrality as business principle. The Compact doesn't take sides, doesn't judge cargo, and doesn't ask questions. They believe that the tunnels are neutral ground — a Switzerland beneath Detroit — and that this neutrality is what keeps them alive and profitable. Breaking neutrality is the one unforgivable sin.
territory: Detroit's underground salt mine tunnel network, with access points at the waterfront, Midtown, and the Corktown industrial zone.
methods: Tunnel smuggling — moving goods and people through underground passages that bypass all surface monitoring
Guided transit — providing experienced guides through a tunnel network that's lethal to the uninitiated
Passage maintenance — continuous repair and reinforcement of tunnel routes to keep them navigable
Access control — fortified entry points with guards who verify clients and payment before admission
Route secrecy — deliberately collapsing abandoned passages to prevent unauthorized exploration
Emergency extraction — offering rapid underground evacuation for clients willing to pay emergency rates
resources: An extensive tunnel network beneath Detroit connecting the waterfront to interior districts
Fifty experienced members including tunnel guides, guards, and maintenance specialists
Fortified access points at three major entry locations
Detailed maps of the tunnel system — the Compact's most closely guarded asset
Relationships with every faction that needs to move goods through Detroit
A perfect safety record for guided transits — reputation as reliable and professional
story_hooks: Someone collapsed a section of the tunnel network deliberately — the Compact suspects sabotage from a surface-level competitor
A client being smuggled through the tunnels turns out to be far more valuable — and dangerous — than advertised
The Compact's tunnel maps have been stolen, and whoever has them could destroy the entire network
A tunnel expansion broke into something sealed — a pre-collapse facility that was buried for a reason
Axiom Security is pressuring the Compact to become an intelligence asset — report who moves through, or be shut down
